cards.text: Amos, a shepherd from Tekoa, has a message from God for Israel (Amos 1:1). God has sent trouble after trouble, and every time, Israel did not return to Him (Amos 4:6-11). Now Amos calls out, 'Hear this word, O house of Israel,' and he takes up something against them.

cards.question: What does Amos take up against the house of Israel?

cards.text: Here's how it opens: 'Fallen is Virgin Israel.' Friend, that's giving the eulogy while the guy is sitting in the front row LISTENING.

cards.question: Amos says fallen Israel lies abandoned on her land, with ___ to raise her up.

cards.text: No one. Never to rise again. Then the Lord GOD speaks, and He's counting what happens when the cities of Israel march out.

cards.question: A city in Israel marches out a thousand strong. How many will it have left?
And the city that marches out a hundred strong? True or false: It will have just ten left.

cards.text: Then the LORD speaks to the house of Israel. After all that? Friend, I had my mustache over my EYES.

cards.question: What does the LORD tell the house of Israel?

cards.text: Then He gets specific: don't seek Bethel, don't go to Gilgal, don't journey to Beersheba. Seeking those places instead of Him is like getting invited to a friend's house and spending the whole night hugging the front door.

cards.question: Gilgal is one of the places God tells Israel not to go. God says Gilgal will surely go into ___.

cards.text: And Bethel will come to nothing. Then the call comes again: seek the LORD and live, or He will sweep through the house of Joseph, the families that came from Joseph.

cards.question: If they don't seek Him, the LORD will sweep through the house of Joseph like what?
That fire will devour everything. True or false: Someone at Bethel will be able to put it out.

cards.text: Then the LORD calls out a group of people: 'There are those who turn justice into wormwood and cast righteousness to the ground.'

Then comes a picture of who the LORD is: He made the Pleiades and Orion. Friend, every cookie box we seal lights ONE star in my sky, and I take a victory lap on my base every time, but He made whole constellations.

cards.question: True or false: The One who made the Pleiades and Orion also turns darkness into dawn and pours the waters of the sea over the earth.

cards.text: And this same God has something to say about the strong and their stronghold.

cards.question: True or false: The strong will be safe from the LORD inside their stronghold.

cards.text: Then the LORD calls out another group: 'There are those who hate the one who reproves in the gate and despise him who speaks with integrity.' Friend, that's getting MAD at the smoke detector.
Then comes a therefore: they trample on the poor and take a tax of grain from him. And they've built stone houses.

cards.question: What does God say about the stone houses they've built?

answers.text: They will never live in them
They will go to the poor

cards.question: They've planted lush vineyards too. True or false: They'll get to drink the wine from them.

cards.text: Build it and never live in it, which is like stamping a whole batch and never getting ONE cookie. Then the LORD says, 'For I know that your transgressions are many and your sins are numerous.'

cards.question: The LORD says they oppress the righteous. How?
And in the gate, they deprive the poor of ___.

cards.text: Then comes a line about the prudent, and what they do when the days are this evil.

cards.question: True or false: In days this evil, the prudent speak up loudly.

cards.text: But the call comes back again: 'Seek good, not evil, so that you may live.' Different words, same heartbeat as 'Seek Me and live!'

cards.question: If Israel seeks good, what does Amos say the LORD, the God of Hosts, will do?

answers.text: He will give them a king

cards.question: The LORD keeps calling to the house of Israel: 'Hate ___ and love ___; establish justice in the gate.'

cards.text: Then comes one little word: perhaps. Friend, I spent years in a junk drawer holding my breath every time the light came in, so trust me, a perhaps from God is a BIG word.

cards.question: Perhaps the LORD, the God of Hosts, will be gracious to whom?

cards.text: Then the LORD, the God of Hosts, the Lord, says what's coming: wailing in all the public squares and cries of 'Alas! Alas!' in all the streets.

cards.question: True or false: Even the farmer will be summoned to mourn.

cards.text: And it doesn't stay in the streets. There will be wailing in all the vineyards too.

cards.question: Why does the LORD say there will be wailing in all the vineyards?

answers.text: He will pass through their midst
He will hide His face from them
He will send a famine on them

findings.problem: The question says Amos is the one speaking in Amos 5:14 ('what does Amos say the LORD... will do'). In the BSB, the LORD's quoted speech opens at 5:4 and closes at the end of 5:15, so 5:14 is part of what the LORD says. The very next card (card 12) credits 5:15, part of the same speech, to the LORD. The two cards contradict each other, and the text shows card 11's speaker is wrong.

rule.text: Papa Dorin can retell in his own words and fill in what the text clearly implies. Scene-setting details are fine. He never says anything the text shows is wrong.

findings.problem: Amos 5:14 says the LORD will be with them 'as you have claimed.' No card tells the baker this, so they miss an important detail: Israel already claims the LORD is with them.

rule.text: When the baker leaves Prep, they understand the whole passage without missing an important detail.

findings.problem: Card 10 is a story card, and it quotes 'Seek good, not evil' (Amos 5:14) right before this fill in the blank. That nearly hands the baker 'Hate evil and love good' (Amos 5:15), so the blanks test the wording of the line instead of meaning the baker reasons out. The give-away comes from a story card, not from a choice the baker has already answered, so it isn't an allowed easy follow-up.

rule.text: No card ever gives away the answer to a choice card that comes later.

findings.problem: The card says God 'has something to say about the strong and their stronghold.' Amos 5:9 doesn't show Him saying anything here. It describes what He does: He flashes destruction on the strong, so that fury comes upon the stronghold.

rule.text: Call things what the text calls them.
